subject: Third-party processor onboarding notice — objection deadline & e-sign path
messages:
From: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@acmecloud.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Notification: onboarding of Acme Analytics (third-party processor)

Hi Sean / Laura,

As part of a routine update to our provider stack, we wanted to notify Redwood that we've engaged Acme Analytics (subsidiary of AcmeCloud) to provide anonymized telemetry enrichment. Per our existing DPA, we're sending the subprocessor notice and an addendum for signature.

Key details:
- Processor name: Acme Analytics, Inc.
- Processing locations: EU (Ireland) + US (us-west-2)
- Purpose: telemetry enrichment (non-identifying logs)
- Intended access: pseudonymized event data only

Please review and let us know if Redwood has objections within 30 calendar days from receipt. We attached the current subprocessor list and a draft addendum for signature via DocuSign.

Attachments: acme-analytics-subprocessor-list.csv (CSV), dpa-subprocessor-addendum-draft.pdf (PDF)
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/1234-abcdef

Thanks,
Elaine Morris
Sr. Procurement Manager | AcmeCloud
elaine.morris@acmecloud.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@acmecloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notification: onboarding of Acme Analytics (third-party processor)

Elaine — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Looping in Legal (Dev) and Security (Kim) for review. A couple quick asks while they review:

- Can Acme confirm whether standard SCCs will be applied for cross-border processing and which template they rely on?
- Is there any sub-subcontracting planned (i.e., will Acme Analytics use other vendors)? If yes, can we get names/purposes?
- Given our scale, we typically request a 45-day notification window for new subprocessors; your note references 30 days. Is that flexible?

We'll aim to return a consolidated response within 5 business days. If legal or security needs to raise an objection we'll flag it before the expiration window.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

From: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@acmecloud.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notification: onboarding of Acme Analytics (third-party processor)

Sean — thanks for the quick reply. Answers below:

- SCCs: Yes, we will apply the EU SCCs (2021 standard contractual clauses) for EU-to-US transfers. We can attach the signed SCCs once countersigned.
- Sub-subcontracting: Acme Analytics uses CloudEnrich for some enrichment work; CloudEnrich will not receive raw PII and will process only pseudonymized event batches. We have included CloudEnrich on the attached CSV.
- Notification window: Our standard policy is 30 days; we can accept an extended 45-day window for customers who request it, but it requires a short amendment to the addendum. If Redwood prefers 45 days, we can prepare a one-line change and re-send via DocuSign.

DocuSign link (current addendum): https://www.docusign.com/recipient/1234-abcdef

Let me know if you want us to update to 45 days — we can do that today.

Regards,
Elaine Morris
Sr. Procurement Manager | AcmeCloud

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Notification: onboarding of Acme Analytics (third-party processor)

Dev / Kim — forwarding Acme's notice. Quick read: they already named CloudEnrich (we'll need the contract flow and assurances), and they offered to change the notification window to 45 days if we prefer.

Can you please advise:
- Legal: any redlines we should request in the addendum (SCC confirmation, right to audit clause, subprocessor chaining limits)?
- Security: any objections on the CloudEnrich dependency or data residency?

If no major blockers, Sean: happy to move ahead with request for 45 days so we have extra runway for procurement review.

On Wed, Apr 7, 2027 at 08:50 Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@acmecloud.com> wrote:

> - Sub-subcontracting: Acme Analytics uses CloudEnrich for some enrichment work; CloudEnrich will not receive raw PII and will process only pseudonymized event batches. We have included CloudEnrich on the attached CSV.
> - Notification window: Our standard policy is 30 days; we can accept an extended 45-day window for customers who request it, but it requires a short amendment to the addendum.

Thanks,
Laura

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@acmecloud.com>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notification: onboarding of Acme Analytics (third-party processor) — Redwood position and e-sign

Elaine / Acme procurement team — thanks for the clarifications and for offering the 45-day amendment. Redwood is comfortable with Acme Analytics onboarding under the following conditions:

1) Amend the addendum to state a 45-calendar-day objection window (one-line change).
2) Confirm CloudEnrich's role is limited to pseudonymized enrichment and provide their SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent.
3) Confirm SCCs will be executed and attach a copy of the SCCs prior to activation.

If you can update the addendum to reflect item (1), and upload CloudEnrich's compliance evidence, we're happy to sign the addendum via the DocuSign link. We will not raise an objection provided the evidence is received within the 45-day window.

DocuSign (please re-send with the 45-day amendment): https://www.docusign.com/recipient/1234-abcdef

Regards,
Dev Patel
Counsel, Privacy & Contracts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: requested-evidence-checklist.txt]
